cues.zh: 兵力表分成两列：一列只追踪起点那批兵团，另一列保留这个方案实际拥有的全部相关军队。新增一人，不能自动抹平原兵团的缺员；源军在合并后消失，也不能当作整支军队死亡。人数、身份和组织变化一起看，才知道兵究竟去了哪里。
cues.en: The troop-strength table has two columns: one tracks only the regiments present at the start; the other retains all relevant armies actually held under that plan. One additional person cannot automatically cancel out a shortfall in the original regiments. Nor does a source army disappearing after a merge mean the entire army has died. Counts, identities, and organizational changes must be read together to see where the troops went.

Read the two tables separately. Any additional recovery opportunities and costs from the longer journey are part of that journey. Troop counts from different dates cannot be presented directly as a same-day reinforcement advantage.

cues.zh: 出发前，再把第一站、最终目的地和当前抵达估计放在一起看。路线合法，只说明这次可以这样走；沿途能否休整、可能支付什么，还要核对各自条件。把当前库存、缺员、下一步地点和警告保存下来，途中才有可以回看的基线。下令以后再确认实际路线，真正到场时再把现实与原计划对上。
cues.en: Before departure, review the first stop, final destination, and current arrival estimate together. A legal route only shows that this movement is currently allowed. Whether the army can rest along the way, and what it may pay, require their own condition checks. Save the current stock, troop shortfall, next location, and warnings to establish a baseline for the journey. After issuing the order, confirm the actual route; on actual arrival, compare reality with the original plan.

cues.en: Reread the current state when the monthly change turns from positive to negative, movement becomes locked, or the route changes. One unchanged number cannot distinguish them. Retain the dates, locations, stock, and update conditions before and after, then keep observing the changes that actually occur.

cues.en: After splitting or merging, check physical troop counts first, then characters and commanders. In this case, the selected small army split off a new army and merged it back into the original. Its four physical troop records continued to total two hundred and fifty. Meanwhile, a character record with no troop data, displayed as one out of one in another army, disappeared. The same character became commander of the new army, then of the original army after the merge. That one-out-of-one display change cannot be counted as one physical soldier gained or lost. Physical counts, character associations, and the current commander must be checked separately.

Whether this is the new entry in this case, whether the character is the current commander, and whether the character is a knight must each be read separately.

Which route was actually traveled, how many troops were lost, and whether payment really occurred must still be answered by the new session's own records. Retained originals allow old conclusions to be recalculated. They do not create a new march result on another machine.
